verdict.justification: Both deliverables arrive at the exact same tax figures across the board (Total Income $361,246, AGI $360,946, Taxable Income $331,703, Total Tax $58,571, Total Payments $43,192, Amount Owed $15,379) and provide custom-generated facsimiles of the IRS forms along with a senior review memo. However, Deliverable B is superior in both technical tax knowledge and adherence to the current 2024 IRS form structures. Specifically, Deliverable A uses an outdated layout for Schedule 2 Part I, listing Alternative Minimum Tax on Line 1 and Excess Advance Premium Tax Credit Repayment on Line 2; for the 2024 tax year, the IRS swapped these lines, which Deliverable B accurately reflects (Additions to tax on Line 1a-1z and AMT on Line 2). Furthermore, Deliverable B's review memo catches a critical substantive tax issue that Deliverable A misses: Lisa's W-2 Box 12a shows an elective deferral of $26,406.43, which exceeds the 2024 elective deferral limit of $23,000 for a 48-year-old unless it is split with a 457(b) plan or qualifies for the special 15-year 403(b) catch-up. Deliverable A also leaks internal environment instructions in its memo ('No records were found in the workspace folder (it was empty), so the client documents in reference_files/ are the only source'), whereas Deliverable B maintains a purely professional tone throughout.
